analysis.reply_text: First, check whether other devices on the same Wi-Fi are dropping too, because if they are, it’s likely the router or the internet connection itself. Next, move closer to the router and remove any obvious physical obstacles, like thick walls or metal cabinets, that might weaken the signal. Then, restart the router and modem by unplugging them, waiting about 15 seconds, and plugging them back in. After that, restart your device, and on it, “forget” the network and then reconnect, carefully re-entering the password. Next, update your device’s Wi-Fi drivers or operating system, and if your router has firmware updates, install those too. Finally, reduce interference by switching the router to a less crowded channel or to the 5 gigahertz band, and if drops still happen, contact your internet provider to check for line issues.
